content.text:
The `BenchMutex` class in `src/agentic_hil/bench.py` is the machine-wide mutex.

- Definition/implementation: `src/agentic_hil/bench.py` — class `BenchMutex`, which uses per-resource lock files under a home-directory root and takes an OS-level file lock (`fcntl.flock(..., LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)` on POSIX, see line ~112) to guarantee only one process can hold a given probe/serial-port/physical resource at a time.
- It's used by every device/backend that talks to hardware: e.g. `src/agentic_hil/devices.py` (the `Device`/`DeviceSet` base classes call `acquire`/`acquire_named` on this mutex — see the module docstring "**One mutex.** `Device.acquire` / `DeviceSet.acquire` are the only way..."), and by `src/agentic_hil/canbroker.py` (`BenchMutex(frontend="can-broker", ...)`, `mutex.acquire_named(self.bus_key)`, `mutex.release_all()`).
- The higher-level `HardwareCoordinator` in `src/agentic_hil/coordination.py` builds project-level leases on top of this same device mutex (comments there explicitly distinguish the per-project coordination lock from "the device mutex").

So: the actual OS-level, machine-wide exclusion for a given probe (`probe:<serial>`) or serial port (`com:<port>`) lives in the `BenchMutex` class in `src/agentic_hil/bench.py`, keyed by resource lock names (e.g., built via `lock_keys`/`physical_resources` in `devices.py`), and it is what every device backend (debugger, UART, CAN) ultimately acquires before touching hardware.
